# Common Dialogs {#sec-common-dialogs}

The dialogs in this chapter are shown from several places in the program.

## Select Variables {#sec-select-variables-dlg}

The **Select Variables** dialog chooses which columns from a dataset a graph or transformation should use.
For example, a graph may need a list of questions and an optional grouping variable.

**Variables**: This list shows the dataset's columns that have not been selected yet.
Each column's icon shows its data type:

- **Continuous**: Floating-point numbers or a wide range of integers.
- **Categorical**: Text.
- **Discrete**: Integers that represent codes (e.g., *1* = *Agree*).
- **Date**: Dates.
- **Dichotomous (Categorical)**: Text with exactly two distinct values.
- **Dichotomous (Discrete)**: Integers with exactly two distinct values.

To the right of the **Variables** list are one or more lists for the variables the graph needs (e.g., **Questions** or **Grouping**).
Lists marked **(optional)** can be left empty.

To move a variable into a list, select it and click the right-arrow button next to that list.
To move a variable back out of a list, select it and click the left-arrow button.
You can also double-click a variable to move it into the next appropriate empty variable list.

::: {.notesection data-latex=""}
Some lists only accept one variable, and some only accept certain data types.
A warning will be shown if you try to move a variable into a list that cannot accept it.
Also, a variable must be moved into every required list before you can click `r keys("OK")`.
:::

## Sort Columns {#sec-sort-columns-dlg}

The **Sort Columns** dialog sorts a list by one or more of its columns.

**Sort by**: The first row in this grid is the column that the list is sorted by.

**...then by**: The following rows are the columns used to sort rows that have the same value in the previous column.

Double-click a field in the grid to add or edit a sort criterion.
For each criterion, select the **Column** to sort by and its **Order**:

- **Smallest to Largest**: Sorts the column in ascending order.
- **Largest to Smallest**: Sorts the column in descending order.

## View Item {#sec-view-item-dlg}

The **View Item** dialog shows the contents of a row from a list.
To open it, double-click a row in a list (or select the row and press `r keys("Enter")`).

Each of the row's values is shown next to its **Column Name**.
The values cannot be edited, but they can be selected so that portions of their text can be copied.

**Copy**: Click this button to copy the selected values to the clipboard.

**Close**: Click this button to close the dialog.
